title: English for Accounting
overview: English for Accounting is a specialized language development course designed to help accounting and finance professionals communicate accurately and confidently in English. Through authentic accounting documents, workplace scenarios and guided language practice, participants strengthen the terminology and communication skills required to explain financial information, discuss transactions, prepare correspondence, contribute to meetings and interact with colleagues, clients and auditors. The course develops practical language competence rather than providing technical accounting certification.
audience: Accountants, junior accountants, bookkeepers and accounting assistants.
Accounts payable, accounts receivable, payroll and billing personnel.
Finance officers, administrative staff and professionals who use English in accounting-related work.
Accounting students and early-career professionals seeking workplace communication skills.
methodology: Interactive language instruction combines accounting vocabulary workshops, listening and reading tasks, guided speaking practice, role-play, document interpretation, email-writing exercises, simulated finance meetings and short presentations. Participants work with realistic but simplified financial records, receive corrective feedback and complete an integrated workplace communication task.
competencies: Use accounting and financial terminology accurately in professional English.
Read and interpret routine accounting documents and financial summaries.
Explain figures, transactions, variances and payment issues clearly.
Write concise, professional accounting emails, requests and follow-up messages.
Participate confidently in finance discussions, calls and meetings.
Communicate appropriately with internal stakeholders, customers, suppliers and auditors.
objectivesIntro: By the end of the course, participants will be able to:
objectives: Identify and use essential accounting vocabulary and common financial expressions.
Describe accounting functions, business transactions and routine finance processes in English.
Read invoices, receipts, statements and basic financial reports for relevant information.
Explain financial figures, trends and variances using clear, accurate language.
Draft professional emails concerning payments, reconciliations, documentation and deadlines.
Ask for clarification, resolve discrepancies and respond to accounting queries.
Participate in accounting meetings and present concise financial updates.
Apply professional tone, accuracy and confidentiality when communicating financial information.
